nina: Quick RFC follow-up — proposing a minimal operator handshake for private endpoints to reduce cross-account IAM and make upgrades non-disruptive. sketch below.
omar: what's in the minimal payload?
nina: tenant_id, short_lived_operator_token, callback_url, and a small capabilities list. operator fetches full config after the control-channel is established.
lucy: cold-start concern — extra fetch on bootstrap. can we ETag snapshots so operators cache config and avoid repeated full fetchs?
chris: security: operator must never get raw customer keys. plan to issue short-lived client certs signed by our CP CA for mTLS to the control channel; provide cert-sync endpoint for rotation.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: feature-flag operator_onboard_minimal enabled in staging (canary group: 10 tenants) :rocket:
omar: rollout idea — accept both legacy and minimal payloads for 6 weeks; response includes negotiated_version. also return header X-Compat-Mode with ttl so operator can temporarily enable legacy semantics if dataplane checks fail.
nina: acceptance criteria for canary: handshake error rate <0.2% over 48h and median handshake latency improvement >= 10%. i'll draft migration playbook, machine-readable failure codes (AUTH_EXPIRED, MALFORMED_CAPS, DATAPLANE_INCOMPAT), and audit logging requirements. pinging sec + infra for review.
